name: Google enhanced conversions
plain: Google matches a hashed email or phone from a checkout to a Google account to count the sale.
meaning: Advertiser sends SHA-256 normalised email, phone, name and address after a conversion. Google matches them to signed in accounts that clicked an ad. It does not need third party cookies and it works after the person leaves.

web.api: gtag('set','user_data',...); enhanced conversions for web or leads

access.persistence: Conversion window up to 90 days for clicks
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can match a scrambled email or phone from your checkout to a Google account
limits.user_action: You enter your email or phone at checkout or on a form
can: Scramble your email or phone in the browser
Send it to Google to match with a Google account
Count the sale or sign up to the ad that led to it
cannot: Match you if you were not signed in to Google anywhere, or use a different email
Send the plain email or phone
Run if the site does not use the feature
Work if the script is blocked

story.what_it_is: Google matches a scrambled email or phone from your checkout to your Google account to count the sale.

marketing.name: Enhanced conversions
marketing.pitch: Google pitches it as a way to improve measurement by using hashed first party data, with privacy safe matching.

story.for_you: You buy something and the shop sends a scrambled email or phone to Google. Google checks whether you clicked an ad while signed in. You do not see it, and it works after you leave the site.
story.for_makers: It fixes lost sales when cookies are blocked. Matching to signed in accounts gives Google better data to bid with. Advertisers see more sales credited to ads, which supports more spend.

use_cases.example: You click a Google ad on your phone, buy on your laptop, and the shop's scrambled email lets Google link both.
A retailer sends hashed email, name and address at checkout to count sales that cookies miss.
A game store sends a hashed email at purchase so Google Ads can find more players like the buyers.
A marketer sees conversion counts rise, and bid rules improve.
A B2B form sends a hashed work email, so Google can credit the ad that led to a demo request.
Teams check that no plain email is sent, since Google needs it to be hashed first.

risks: Links your sale to your Google account

technical_bounds: Needs advertiser to collect email or phone
Hashing is SHA-256 after trim and lowercase
Consent Mode and law still apply

abuse: Linking checkout identity to Google accounts
